title: Whether Whole-Series Metadata Edits Propagate to Existing Overrides
question: When a whole series is edited (recurrence_id=None) to change non-schedule properties such as SUMMARY, LOCATION, or STATUS, are the changed properties also applied to existing override components that remain valid?
spec_gap: In JSCalendar an override is a patch over the main object, so an unpatched property follows the main object automatically while a patched property keeps its override value. iCalendar override components are full copies with no record of which properties were customized, so a store must choose between copying the change into overrides or leaving them alone. RFC 5546 only notes that instance-specific information is lost on an entire rescheduling unless it is explicitly included; it does not address metadata-only edits.

citations.verbatim_quote: By default, an occurrence inherits all properties from the main object except the start (or due) date-time, which is shifted to match the recurrence id LocalDateTime.
Note that since this is an entire rescheduling of the event, any instance-specific information will be lost, unless explicitly included with the update "REQUEST".

options.summary: Properties explicitly present in the whole-series patch are also written to every valid override; properties absent from the patch, and each override's schedule (DTSTART, DTEND, DUE, DURATION, RECURRENCE-ID), are left as they are.
consequences: Approximates JSCalendar inheritance for the edited properties.
An override that had customized a property in the patch (for example, its own SUMMARY) loses that customization.

options.summary: Only the master component is updated; override components are left unchanged.
consequences: Overridden instances keep stale series-wide values (for example, the old SUMMARY) until edited individually.
